checkCount() - Static method in class com.xpe.client.api.items.CoalBag
The one call that goes and finds out. Clicks Check and waits up to 2.5 seconds for the game to answer. Returns the count, or -1 if no bag is carried. If the game says nothing in time it logs that and returns whatever it knew before. XPE method.
forget() - Static method in class com.xpe.client.api.items.CoalBag
Drops the tracked count back to -1, for a script that knows the bag changed behind its back. contains and isEm pty while unknown. Both answer false, which is the safe direction for contains and the surprising one for isEmpty. An unknown bag is never reported as empty. Test count() == -1 yourself when you need to tell "unknown" apart from "empty". Moving coal. XPE method.
fill() - Static method in class com.xpe.client.api.items.CoalBag
Fills the bag. From the bank when the bank is open, otherwise from the inventory. XPE method.
empty() - Static method in class com.xpe.client.api.items.CoalBag
Empties the bag. Into the bank when the bank is open, otherwise into the inventory. The return value is "did anything move".false m eans nothing shifted: the bag was already full, there was no coal to take, or there was nowhere to put it. Both calls keep the tracked count in step by m easuring the difference. The bank behaviour is the game's, not an extra step. A coal bag's own Fill and Em pty act on the bank whenever the bank interface is open, so a banking script calls empty() with the bank open and the coal goes straight in. Opening and closing An open coal bag is a separate item , and m ining with it open needs no clicks. XPE method.
open() - Static method in class com.xpe.client.api.items.CoalBag
Opens a closed bag, so mined coal goes into it automatically. XPE method.
close() - Static method in class com.xpe.client.api.items.CoalBag
Closes an open bag. Two items, one bag. The open kind is nam ed Open coal bag. bag() and has() find either; isOpen() tells them apart. XPE method.

storeAll() - Static method in class com.xpe.client.api.items.RunePouch
Stores every carried rune kind the pouch will take. Amounts. An amount at or above what is available m oves everything, so Integer.MAX_VALUE m eans "all". The exact value also picks the route the move takes: 1 and 5 use the fixed m enu rows, anything else types the number into the X prompt, and "everything" uses the All row. W hen a store refuses.store returns false without clicking anything if the inventory carries none of that rune, or if the pouch holds no such rune already and every slot is occupied by something else. The reason is logged. Check with contains(rune) || emptySlots() > 0 before storing a kind the pouch may not have room for. XPE method.

close() - Static method in class com.xpe.client.api.items.RunePouch
Closes it. Already closed counts as success. XPE method.
lastAction() - Static method in class com.xpe.client.api.items.RunePouch
The menu action the last move used, such as "Store-5" or "Withdraw-All". W hy lastAction exists. The amount decides which of the four rows a move takes, so a move can net out perfectly correct while having gone by a route you did not intend. This reports the row that actually ran. It is what the built-in test rig asserts, and the first thing worth printing when a move behaves oddly. XPE method.

SilverCrafting - Class in org.dreambot.api.methods.widget.helpers
The furnace's silver panel: opal, jade and topaz rings, necklaces, amulets and bracelets from a silver bar, a mould and a gem, and the single silver items beside them. XPE only, beside Jewellery for gold. DreamBot has no equivalent. Every member is static, and nothing throws: a call that cannot do what was asked returns false and says why in the log. Three things this panel does differently Each of these was m easured on a live panel, and each is why the class looks the way it does. If you have used ItemProcessing, Jewellery or Smithing, these are the three places this one will surprise you.

setSelectedQuantity(int) - Static method in class org.dreambot.api.methods.widget.helpers.SilverCrafting
Selects a quantity by its button and waits for the panel to show it. 1, -1 for All, or a number the panel has a button for. Anything else is refused without a click, and the log nam es the buttons that are there. The panel adds buttons as you carry m ore silver bars. Seen on a live panel: SILVER BARS CARRIED BUTTONS SHOWN 5 1, X, All 6 1, 5, X, All 12 1, 5, 10, X, All SilverCrafting.setSelectedQuantity(7): the silver panel has buttons [1, 5, 10, X, All] and none for 7, and it is not driven through its X prompt - a typed quantity does not show on the panel, so it cannot be confirmed. Nothing was clicked. W hy not X. It was tried twice, with 5 and with 7: the prompt opened, the number was typed and taken, the game said nothing, and nothing on the panel changed. X still read "X" and All stayed lit. That is also what a person sees doing it by hand. A quantity that cannot be read back cannot be confirm ed, and m aking an unconfirm ed number of things is worse than refusing. XPE method.
